leader.name: Arthur Hale
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.biography: A barrister and former chancellor who inherited a government committed to collective security and a defence budget it cannot afford to expand quickly. Hale believes the country's strength lies in the empire, the fleet and the American connection.

traits.name: Parliamentary Mandate
traits.description: Stability is high, but war support grows slowly.

traits.name: Imperial Commitments
traits.description: Manpower must also garrison overseas stations.

parties.name: Conservative Union
parties.description: The largest party in the national government, divided between rearmers and supporters of appeasement.

parties.name: Labour Party
parties.description: Opposes rearmament in principle but supports collective security and public housing.

parties.name: Liberal Party
parties.description: A small parliamentary group with influence in the press and the civil service.

parties.name: Communist Party
parties.description: A narrow industrial base, closely watched by the security service.

advisors.name: Sir James Harrow
advisors.description: Permanent Under-Secretary at the Foreign Office and the architect of the government's collective security line.

advisors.name: Ellen Marsh
advisors.description: A former housing minister with strong links to the unions; she can quiet labour unrest at a price.

advisors.name: General Edmund Carey
advisors.position: Chief of the Imperial General Staff
advisors.description: A cautious staff chief who insists that any continental commitment be matched by shipping and supply.

advisors.name: Cecil Ashdown
advisors.description: Runs the foreign section from a suite in Whitehall; his intercept service is the finest in Europe.

advisors.name: Dr. Martin Tyler
advisors.description: An air power theorist arguing that the next war will be decided by radar, fighters and a trained reserve of pilots.

modifiers.name: Imperial Preference
modifiers.description: Trade inside the sterling area supplies rubber, tin and food at preferential rates.

modifiers.name: Ten Year Rule
modifiers.description: The treasury still plans on the assumption that no major war will occur within a decade.

modifiers.name: Air Defence of Great Britain
modifiers.description: A chain of radar stations and observer corps covers the eastern approaches.

decisions.name: Shadow Factory Scheme
decisions.description: License civilian plants to build aero engines and airframes in peacetime, under government guarantee.

decisions.name: Chain Home Expansion
decisions.description: Extend radar coverage along the east coast and integrate it with the fighter control rooms.

decisions.name: Local Defence Volunteers
decisions.description: Raise a part-time home defence force from men outside the conscription age bands.

decisions.name: Commonwealth Consultation
decisions.description: Convene the dominion prime ministers to coordinate war plans and imperial supply.

decisions.name: Public Housing Act
decisions.description: Fund slum clearance and new council housing to honour the government's domestic promises.

agency.name: Secret Intelligence Service
agency.description: The foreign intelligence service, with stations across Europe and a growing signals section at Bletchley.
